newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: T-bill yields rise as sellers swamp secondary mkt.
newsitem.headline: T-bill yields rise as sellers swamp secondary mkt.

text.p: Yields of Philippine Treasury bills were firmer in the secondary market as banks dumped their holdings on fears that domestic rates would rise further amid sporadic attacks on the peso, traders said.
"A lot of banks were unloading their holdings. They would rather invest in short-term reverse repos which offer much better rates," one fixed-income securities trader at a finance company said.
The Central Bank had kept its benchmark overnight borrowing rate at 30 percent in an effort to ward speculators off the local currency.
The peso came under fresh speculative selling early on Wednesday after the Singapore Straits Times said the Philippine Central Bank's Monetary Board was set to discuss the issue of peso devaluation.
Trade Minister Cesar Bautista, to whom the information was attributed, denied the report.

"The secondary T-bill market is still bearish," added another trader at a large commercial bank. He said holders of T-bills were selling bills in anticipation of a further rate hike due to the instability in the foreign exchange market.
Banks were quoting three-month bills between 12.15 to 12.50, six-month bills between 12.375 to 12.75, one-year bills at 12.80 to 13.25 percent.
Most of the rates were higher than the average rates posted in the latest auction.

The interbank call loan market was likewise active with done rates ranging from a low of 30.03125 percent to a high of 36 percent. Average rate firmed to 30.375 percent from Tuesday's 30.0625 percent.
